g.title: PICO
g.text: RP2350. New project, so these pins were chosen freely -- no
firmware, only one runs on a chip at a time). SP/CE is a defined
8-pin JST-SH connector -- plugging in the RM2 cable IS the wiring
step, no discrete GPIO wiring needed for WiFi. GPIO19 drives
A4988 ENABLE in software -- see A4988 notes below for why this

g.title: W_SPCE
g.text: SP/CE JST-SH cable (direct plug, comes with the RM2 breakout)

g.title: ENCODER
g.text: Mounted on the stepper shaft. Pin ORDER confirmed on the bench to
match the physical module (GND, CS, CLK, MOSI, MISO, V) -- an
earlier version of this diagram used a different, made-up order
(VCC first), which is suspected to have caused a VCC/GND swap when
wired position-by-position against it. No CAL_EN pin on this
module -- MT6835 User Auto-Calibration isn't available with this
specific breakout; use RUN's constant-rotation linearity capture
instead, which doesn't need it. SPI1 remapped -- see

g.title: A4988
g.text: ENABLE is wired to Pico GPIO19, NOT jumpered to GND_LOGIC --
confirmed on the bench that hardwiring it always-enabled prevented
the motor from stepping (even with STEP/DIR pulses verified
correct); holding it disabled through boot/WiFi connect and
enabling only afterward (see EncoderCalibration.ino setup()) fixed
it reliably. Remaining on-board jumpers (not drawn as wires --
adjacent-pin bridges on the A4988 module itself, not inter-module
wiring): RESET jumpered to SLEEP, that joined pair tied to VDD (out
of reset/not sleeping); MS1=HIGH, MS2=HIGH, MS3=LOW for 1/8
microstep (tie MS1/MS2 to VDD, MS3 to GND_LOGIC) -- a reasonable
default for smooth rotation; full step (all three to GND_LOGIC)
also works fine since the encoder, not the driver's own microstep
count, is the ground truth here.
REQUIRED: a low-ESR electrolytic capacitor (47uF or more, rated above
your motor PSU voltage) across VMOT/GND_MOTOR, close to the board --
Pololu's own A4988 boards do NOT include this on-board, and without
it, inductive voltage spikes from the stepper coils can damage the

g.title: MOTOR_PSU
g.text: Separate from the Pico's own power, same reasoning as the SBUS
rig's servo PSU. Steppers are current-driven, not voltage-driven --
the A4988 regulates coil current via chopping regardless of supply
voltage, so 12V is a normal, safe choice even though the motor's
own voltage rating differs; what actually matters is setting the
A4988's current-limit trimpot correctly for this motor's 1.68A/phase
rating (see chat notes -- VREF = I_limit x 8 x R_sense, verify with
a multimeter BEFORE connecting the motor).

g.title: W_MOTOR_PWR
g.text: motor power (VMOT/GND_MOTOR) -- fit the decoupling capacitor here, see A4988 notes

g.title: W_COMMON_GND
g.text: common ground reference, motor PSU to Pico

g.title: NEMA17
g.text: 1.8deg/step, rated 1.68A/phase. Verify coil pairing with a
multimeter if your unit's wire colours aren't documented --
measure continuity between wire pairs, wires with continuity
between them are the same coil. Wrong pairing (mixing wires from
different coils) causes rough/skipped rotation, not damage.

g.title: RM2
g.text: Pimoroni RM2 Wireless and Bluetooth Breakout
Plugs directly into the Pico's SP/CE connector via its own cable.
